value_stream.name: Supply Chain Finance & Working Capital Management

fields.Participants: Treasury Manager, FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Merchandising (links to VS-101), Supply Chain (links to VS-02), AR/Credit (links to VS-16)
fields.Trigger: Annual planning (links to VS-33.1); treasury/merchandise strategy refresh

workflows.name: Working-Capital KPI Definition, Baseline & Target Setting (DPO/DIO/DSO/DWC)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "accounts payable days" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-file of "Treasury/FP&A baseline current DWC by entity/category/channel using actuals, benchmark" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "CFO/Executive committee approve the DWC targets, decompose into DPO/DIO/DSO" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-546 (ensure controlled execution — Working Capital Analytics & Cash-Conversion-Cycle Governance (PA-105.3).)
- operational: single KPI definition and governance; operational: bottom-up validation with Merchandising/Supply/AR
Pain Points / Risks: - **Definition-inconsistency risk**: Different DPO/DIO definitions across owners distort the target; mitigated by single KPI definition and governance
- **Unrealistic-target risk**: Targets unmoored from operational reality cause dysfunction; mitigated by bottom-up validation with Merchandising/Supply/AR
System Touchpoints: - BI/FP&A planning (links to VS-28.1/VS-17.4); AP/inventory/AR data (links to VS-15/VS-05/VS-16); cash forecast (links to VS-18.1)

steps.activity: Treasury/FP&A define the working-capital KPI set: DPO (accounts payable days), DIO (inventory days), DSO (receivable days), DWC (days working capital = DIO + DSO − DPO), and CCC; establish data sources (AP links to VS-15, inventory links to VS-05, AR links to VS-16) and calculation governance

Treasury/FP&A baseline current DWC by entity/category/channel using actuals, benchmark against retail/home-improvement norms and the 6–8x inventory-turn target (per profile §12.3), and set improvement targets aligned to the cash-flow/EBITDA plan (links to VS-33.1/VS-18.1)

CFO/Executive committee approve the DWC targets, decompose into DPO/DIO/DSO sub-targets by owner (Treasury-AP for DPO, Merchandising-Supply for DIO, AR-Credit for DSO), and establish the monthly review cadence (W3399) and initiative portfolio (W3398)

fields.Participants: Treasury Manager, Procurement Director, AP Manager, Category Managers (links to VS-01)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Treasury/Procurement analyze DPO by vendor/category/segment" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track initiative-by-initiative DPO gain" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Treasury measure DPO movement vs target, isolate drivers" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-546 (ensure controlled execution — Working Capital Analytics & Cash-Conversion-Cycle Governance (PA-105.3).)
- operational: price-for-terms analytics (W3381); operational: SCF access and health screening
Pain Points / Risks: - **Margin-offset risk**: Term extension extracted via price concession erodes margin (links to VS-101.3); mitigated by price-for-terms analytics (W3381)
- **Vendor-harm risk**: Aggressive DPO pushback harms fragile vendors and supply continuity; mitigated by SCF access and health screening
System Touchpoints: - AP/payment-terms master (links to VS-15/W295); SCF platform (links to W3377); spend analytics (links to VS-67/VS-28.1)

steps.activity: Treasury/Procurement analyze DPO by vendor/category/segment: actual vs contracted terms, on-time-payment rate, term-negotiation opportunity, and SCF-eligibility; identify the DPO-improvement backlog (extended terms per W3381, SCF enrollment per W3379, payment-run timing per VS-15.2)

Procurement/Category Managers execute the DPO initiatives: renegotiate terms (W3381), enroll vendors in SCF (W3379), tighten payment-run timing (links to VS-15.2), and resolve term-master data issues (links to W295); track initiative-by-initiative DPO gain

Treasury measure DPO movement vs target, isolate drivers (term change vs payment timing vs SCF), and report to the working-capital review (W3399); re-prioritize the backlog and flag adverse vendor reactions

fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, Merchandise Planners (links to VS-101), Supply Planning (links to VS-02.1), Inventory (links to VS-05), Treasury Manager
fields.Trigger: DWC target (W3393); merchandise plan (links to VS-101)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Merchandising/Supply analyze DIO by department/category/SKU" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "track inventory-$ release" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Treasury/Merchandising measure DIO movement vs target and the 6–8x" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-546 (ensure controlled execution — Working Capital Analytics & Cash-Conversion-Cycle Governance (PA-105.3).)
- operational: ABC-aware targeting and service-level guardrails; operational: OTB control (links to VS-101 W3283)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stockout risk**: Over-aggressive DIO reduction causes lost sales (links to VS-101.3); mitigated by ABC-aware targeting and service-level guardrails
- **Overbuy-offset risk**: DIO gains reversed by undisciplined OTB; mitigated by OTB control (links to VS-101 W3283)
System Touchpoints: - Merchandise planning/OTB (links to VS-101); demand planning (links to VS-02.1); inventory (links to VS-05); cash forecast (links to VS-18.1)

steps.activity: Merchandising/Supply analyze DIO by department/category/SKU: weeks-of-supply vs target, slow-moving/obsolete (links to VS-05.3/W220), overstock, OTB utilization (links to VS-101 W3283), and import-pipeline inventory (links to VS-02.2); identify the DIO cash-release backlog

Merchandising/Supply execute DIO initiatives: tighten OTB (links to VS-101 W3283), reduce safety stock on C-items, accelerate slow-mover clearance (links to VS-64/VS-05.3), optimize import order quantity/lead (links to VS-02.2), and improve forecast accuracy (links to VS-02.1); track inventory-$ release

Treasury/Merchandising measure DIO movement vs target and the 6–8x turn target (per profile §12.3), compute inventory-$ released and its cash impact (links to VS-18.1), and report to the working-capital review (W3399); guard against stockout/margin trade-off (links to VS-101.3)

steps.activity: AR/Credit analyze DSO by customer/segment/channel: actual days vs terms (Net 30 trade / Net 60–90 corporate per profile §10.3), aging (links to VS-16.2), dispute volume, and collection effectiveness; identify the DSO cash-release backlog

AR/Trade execute DSO initiatives: tighten credit terms/limits (links to VS-16.1/VS-68), accelerate collections (links to VS-16.2 W108), resolve disputes faster (links to VS-90/W244), promote e-invoicing/electronic payment (links to VS-80/VS-79), and consider selective receivables financing; track DSO-$ release

Treasury/AR measure DSO movement vs target, compute receivable-$ released and its cash impact (links to VS-18.1), balance against trade-credit-risk appetite (links to VS-68), and report to the working-capital review (W3399)

steps.activity: Treasury/FP&A build/maintain the CCC forecast model: project DPO/DIO/DSO from plan + initiatives (W3394–W3396), compute forward DWC and the resulting cash generation/consumption, and integrate to the rolling cash forecast (links to VS-18.1/W233)

Treasury model scenarios: seasonal peak (ber-months inventory build per profile §13.2), import-pipeline surge (links to VS-02.2), capex acceleration (links to VS-40), supplier-distress (links to VS-68/VS-02.3), and macro/FX shock (links to VS-18.3); quantify CCC and liquidity impact

Treasury/CFO use the CCC forecast to inform SCF facility sizing (W3377/W3382), dynamic-discounting throttle (W3389), debt/facility decisions (links to VS-18/W319), and the board cash outlook (links to VS-36); communicate material CCC shifts to executives

workflows.name: Working-Capital Initiative Portfolio, Prioritization & Benefits Realization

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-collect of "collection acceleration, process automation, etc." (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-assign of "assign executive sponsors" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track benefits realization" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-546 (ensure controlled execution — Working Capital Analytics & Cash-Conversion-Cycle Governance (PA-105.3).)
- operational: rigorous measurement and attribution; operational: executive sponsorship and quarterly review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Benefits-overstatement risk**: Over-claimed benefits distort the cash outlook; mitigated by rigorous measurement and attribution
- **Initiative-stall risk**: Cross-functional initiatives lack an owner and stall; mitigated by executive sponsorship and quarterly review
System Touchpoints: - Portfolio/project tracking; FP&A (links to VS-17.4); BI (links to VS-28.1); IT automation (links to VS-27/VS-30)

steps.activity: Treasury maintain the working-capital initiative portfolio: each initiative (DPO term extension, DIO OTB tightening, DSO collection acceleration, process automation, etc.) with owner, expected cash/benefit, cost, timeline, and risk; intake new ideas continuously

Treasury/CFO prioritize the portfolio by benefit-vs-effort and risk, sequence into quarterly waves, secure resources (incl. IT links to VS-27/VS-30 automation), and assign executive sponsors; resolve cross-functional conflicts (e.g., DPO vs vendor margin per W3381)

FP&A/Treasury track benefits realization: measure actual vs expected cash release per initiative, attribute DWC movement to specific initiatives, and report realization rate to the executive committee (links to VS-33.2) and board (links to VS-36); retire/close or re-baseline initiatives

workflows.name: Working-Capital Policy, Governance & Board-Level Cash Discipline

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "DWC/DPO/DIO/DSO governance, receivables-financing limits" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review working-capital controls" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System rule-based auto-approval of "approve policy updates" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-546 (ensure controlled execution — Working Capital Analytics & Cash-Conversion-Cycle Governance (PA-105.3).)
- operational: audit review (links to VS-21) and SoD; operational: single source and audit sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Control-gap risk**: Weak controls over SCF/discounting enable fraud/error; mitigated by audit review (links to VS-21) and SoD
- **Disclosure-inconsistency risk**: DWC/working-capital disclosures inconsistent with financials; mitigated by single source and audit sign-off
System Touchpoints: - Policy/governance repository (links to VS-88 records/document control); treasury policy (links to VS-18 W322); ERM (links to VS-21.2); audit (links to VS-21); board reporting (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Treasury/CFO maintain the working-capital policy: payment-term standards, SCF/dynamic-discounting authority matrix, DWC/DPO/DIO/DSO governance, receivables-financing limits, inventory-commitment controls (links to VS-101 OTB), and cash-forecast accuracy tolerance; align to the treasury policy (links to VS-18 W322) and risk appetite (links to VS-21.2)

Internal Audit/Risk review working-capital controls: SoD over SCF/dynamic-discounting (links to W3384/W3392), term-change authorization, OTB/markdown controls (links to VS-101), accuracy of DWC KPIs, and off-balance-sheet classification (links to W3377); feed findings to remediation

CFO report working-capital governance, risk, and performance to the Audit Committee/Board (links to VS-36), confirm alignment with the capital/liquidity strategy and EBITDA target, and approve policy updates; ensure disclosure consistency in financial reporting (links to VS-17)

fields.Frequency: Rare; 0–2 stress declarations per year expected (seasonal build + a funding shock is the classic compound scenario)
fields.Participants: Treasury Manager (cash council chair), Finance Controller, VP Merchandising (inventory levers per W3395), AR/Credit Manager (DSO levers per W3396), AP Manager (payment execution per W556), Procurement Director (vendor terms), SCF Program Lead (facility drawdown per W3377/W3382), VP Legal (waiver/cure documentation), Internal Audit (observer), Board/Audit Committee, lenders
fields.Trigger: The 13-week rolling cash forecast breaches the minimum-liquidity floor (days-of-cover floor per the W3400 working-capital policy); W319 covenant monitoring signals headroom < 10% or an actual breach; or a funding-impairment event (W5541 bank failure, W3382 SCF facility suspension) puts the disbursement calendar at risk
fields.Volume: 1 declaration × the full enterprise disbursement calendar (~PHP 5B/month receipts cycle per the W1474 canon) × all funding facilities (revolving credit, W3377 SCF program, W170-class pledge lines) × ~5,200 trade vendors' payment terms

Automation Opportunity: - The forecast engine auto-tests the floor and covenant-headroom triggers daily and drafts the declaration evidence pack with variance attribution (replaces manual Step 1 assembly)
- The payment-prioritization tiering executes as AP-run rules with tier assignments, CFO e-signature on overrides, and full exception logging (replaces manual Step 4 triage)
Background: The steady-state halves are owned — W3393–W3400 run the KPI/forecast/governance cycle and W319 monitors covenant compliance — but no workflow owned the *stressed* state: the declaration decision, the war-room cadence, the lever sequence, the vendor payment-prioritization tiers when cash is insufficient, the lender waiver/cure negotiation, and the governance clock. The failure mode this prevents is a cascade: missed SCF settlements trigger vendor exits (W3383/W3384), priority errors pay discretionary spend while statutory remittances or payroll bounce (the W5540 chain), and an unmanaged covenant breach converts a liquidity event into a default event. This workflow is the escalation canon above those steady-state workflows; it does not replace them — it sequences and overrides them under the declaration.
Controls: - CTL-546 (ensure controlled execution — Working Capital Analytics & Cash-Conversion-Cycle Governance (PA-105.3).); CTL-61 (ensure debt covenant monitoring.)
- operational: statutory wages and government remittances are Tier-1 under any prioritization; tier exceptions require CFO sign-off with logged rationale
- operational: declaration and exit decisions carry documented trigger evidence against the W3400 policy floor
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cascade risk**: a missed SCF settlement or critical-vendor default during stress converts a funding gap into a supply and program crisis; mitigated by Tier-3 protection in Step 4 and the W3384 program-risk linkage
- **Priority-error risk**: discretionary spend paid while statutory wages/remittances bounce; mitigated by the statutory-first tier ordering (Step 4) and CFO-signed exceptions only
- **Silent-breach risk**: a covenant notice lapses unactioned until default; mitigated by the never-lapse rule and certificate calendar in Step 5
- **Disclosure risk**: selective or premature communication to one lender/vendor over others; mitigated by the W5017 disclosure-controls discipline (Step 6)
- **False-exit risk**: stress declared over before the forecast proves durable; mitigated by the 4-consecutive-week exit gate (Step 7)
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed within the existing Treasury, Finance, AP/AR and Legal functions; stress-cadence effort is event-driven and the sensors are the existing W3397/W319 workflows. No incremental headcount.
System Touchpoints: - 13-week rolling cash forecast with daily lock & variance-vs-baseline (treasury workbench; feeds W3397 scenario models)
- Liquidity-floor & covenant-headroom dashboard with declaration/evidence capture (links to W319 monitoring and W3400 policy parameters)
- Payment-prioritization tier flags in the AP run (links to W556; tier overrides carry CFO e-signature)
- Facility-utilization & availability view across revolving, SCF (W3382) and pledge lines (W170)
- OTB/capex freeze gates (links to W101 open-to-buy and W21 capex workflows)
- Board/Audit-Committee pack & disclosure-controls log (links to W5017)
Time Estimate: Standing effort: the W3397 forecast and W319 monitoring already run the steady-state sensors (no added baseline). Under declaration: cash-council cadence ≈ 4–6 staff-hours/day across the council for 4–12 weeks ≈ 120–500 staff-hours per stress event (event-driven, no annual figure claimed); lender waiver work ≈ 40–80 hours Legal/Treasury per facility affected.

steps.activity: **Stress declaration & cash council**: CFO declares stress on the trigger evidence (floor breach, covenant headroom, funding impairment); daily cash council stands up (Treasury chair, Controller, AP, AR/Credit, Procurement, SCF Lead); 13-week forecast re-locked daily with weekly-versus-baseline variance; declaration logged with trigger evidence

**Root-cause & horizon classification**: seasonal (ber-months inventory build vs structural) — seasonal stress borrows against the post-season ramp; structural (margin/composition decay) or event-driven (W5541-class impairment, facility suspension) — class sets which levers are on the table and the exit criteria

**Lever sequence (reversibility-ordered)**: (a) accelerate collections — DSO sprint per W3396 (collection-cadence surge on top-200 AR accounts, credit-hold discipline per W68); (b) draw available committed liquidity — revolving facility, W3382 SCF utilization headroom; (c) stretch payables *within terms* — W3394 DPO levers, negotiated short extensions with critical vendors; (d) release valves — W3395 inventory cash-release (OTB freeze on discretionary buys per W101), W21-class capex deferral gate; (e) last-rung — non-core asset disposals. Each lever has an owner, an expected PHP range, and a decision deadline

**Payment prioritization tiers (when cash < obligations)**: Tier 1 — statutory wages & government remittances (payroll per W10/W5540, SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG/BIR per W1527/W1306); Tier 2 — secured/pledged obligations & LC settlements (W170/W1455 classes — collateral at risk), payroll funding accounts; Tier 3 — critical-supply and SCF-settled vendors (program-exit risk per W3384); Tier 4 — remaining trade payables by criticality and cost-of-default; the AP run executes the tiers, and exceptions require CFO sign-off

**Covenant management**: on breach or headroom < 10% — VP Legal + Treasury open lender engagement (waiver request, cure plan, equity/asset-cure options per the W319 facility terms); no covenant notice is ever allowed to lapse silently; covenant-compliance certificate calendar enforced

**Governance clock & communication**: Audit Committee/Board notified within 5 business days of declaration (and immediately on actual breach); lender disclosures per facility covenants; no selective disclosure per the W5017 canon if material; employee/customer-facing messaging only via approved comms (W855 discipline)

**Exit, floor recalibration & post-mortem**: declare exit when 13-week forecast holds the floor + buffer for 4 consecutive weeks; post-mortem — trigger timing, lever effectiveness vs claimed ranges, KRI threshold recalibration in the VS-21.2 risk register (early-warning lead time), working-capital floor and covenant-headroom policy updates per W3400
